title: Optimal Intravesical Lidocaine Volume for Pain Relief During Office Intra-detrusor Onabotulinum Toxin a Injections
official: Optimal Intravesical Lidocaine Volume for Pain Relief During Office Intra-detrusor Onabotulinum Toxin a Injections: a Prospective Randomized Superiority Trial
summary: The purpose of our study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of different volumes of bladder-numbing medication for pain relief at the time of office bladder Botox injections. This is a randomized prospective, double-blind superiority trial comparing 200 ml 2% lidocaine versus 30 ml 2% lidocaine for office Botox injections.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adult female, \>18 years, English-speaking (surveys utilized are not validated in all languages)
* Able to provide informed consent
* Indications: Refractory urge urinary incontinence, Refractory urinary urgency and frequency, Neurogenic bladder (without sensory deficit)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Untreated urinary tract infection at the time of procedure
* Contra-indication to Botox
* Contraindication to intravesical lidocaine
* Inability to provide informed consent
* Pregnancy, breast-feeding, intending to become pregnant within 6 months of treatment

sites.f: University of Louisville Division of Urogynecology and Reconstructive Pelvic Surgery
